items.title: Section: The Chapter on Discipline Opens — Nine Aspects, the Same Framework as Giving

items.zh: 云何菩薩戒波羅蜜多？嗢拕南曰：自性、一切、難、一切門、善士、一切種、遂求、二世樂、清淨，如是九種相，是名略說戒。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's perfection of discipline? The summarising verse states: intrinsic nature, comprehensiveness, difficulty, universal scope, purity of motive, completeness across every circumstance, responsiveness to what is asked for, benefit in both this life and the next, and freedom from taint — these nine aspects are, in brief, called discipline.

items.zh: 謂九種相戒，名為菩薩戒波羅蜜多。一、自性戒，二、一切戒，三、難行戒，四、一切門戒，五、善士戒，六、一切種戒，七、遂求戒，八、此世他世樂戒，九、清淨戒。
items.en: These nine aspects of discipline are called a bodhisattva's perfection of discipline: first, discipline in its intrinsic nature; second, comprehensive discipline; third, difficult discipline; fourth, discipline through every gateway; fifth, discipline of a genuinely good person; sixth, discipline complete in every kind; seventh, discipline that fulfils what is asked; eighth, discipline that brings joy in this life and the next; ninth, pure discipline.

items.title: Section: Discipline's Intrinsic Nature Opens — Four Defining Qualities

items.zh: 云何菩薩自性戒？謂若略說具四功德，當知是名菩薩自性戒，何等為四？一、從他正受，二、善淨意樂，三、犯已還淨，四、深敬專念無有
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's discipline in its intrinsic nature? In brief, possessing four qualities is what should be understood as a bodhisattva's discipline in its intrinsic nature. What are the four? First, properly received from another; second, a genuinely good and pure aspiration; third, purified again after a lapse; fourth, deep reverence and focused mindfulness with no violation at all.

items.title: Section: Deep Reverence Without Violation — The Rare, Ideal Case

items.zh: 違犯。
items.en: "Deep reverence and focused mindfulness with no violation" means: through a genuinely good and pure aspiration, giving rise to the utmost reverence and respect towards the precepts received. From the very outset, sustaining focused diligence and never losing mindfulness, no violation occurs.

items.title: Section: Four Qualities Regrouped — Shame Before Others, Shame Before Oneself, and Freedom From Lingering Remorse

items.zh: 由諸菩薩從他正受故，於所學戒若有違犯，即外觀他深生愧恥。由諸菩薩善淨意樂故，於所學戒若有違犯，即內自顧深起慚羞。
items.en: Because bodhisattvas properly receive the precepts from another, should they violate what they have learned, they look outward towards that other and feel deep shame before others. Because bodhisattvas hold a genuinely good and pure aspiration, should they violate what they have learned, they look inward at themselves and feel deep shame before themselves.

items.zh: 由諸菩薩於諸學處犯已還淨、深敬專念初無違犯二因緣故，離諸惡作。
items.en: Because bodhisattvas, regarding the precepts, either purify a lapse through confession or, from the very start, hold such deep reverence and focused mindfulness that no violation ever occurs, through these two causes they are freed of lingering remorse.

items.title: Section: Four Qualities Regroup Into Two, Through Three Different Lenses

items.zh: 如是菩薩從他正受、善淨意樂為依止故，生起慚愧；由慚愧故，能善防護所受尸羅；由善防護所受戒故，離諸惡作。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, resting on proper reception and pure aspiration, give rise to a sense of conscience; through that conscience, they are able to skilfully guard the precepts received; and through skilfully guarding the precepts received, they are freed of lingering remorse.

items.zh: 又於是中，從他正受、善淨意樂，此二是法；犯已還淨、深敬專念無有違犯，此二是前二法所引。又於是中，從他正受、善淨意樂、深敬專念無有違犯，由此三法，應知能令不毀菩薩所受淨戒；犯已還淨，由此一法，應知能令犯已還出。
items.en: Further, among these: proper reception and pure aspiration are themselves the underlying substance; purification through confession and unbroken reverence are what these two produce. And further: proper reception, pure aspiration, and unbroken reverence, these three together, should be understood as what keeps the received precepts from ever being violated at all; purification through confession alone should be understood as what restores them once violated.

items.title: Section: The Three Great Storehouses of Discipline — Restraint, Wholesome Practice, Benefiting Beings

items.zh: 如是菩薩具四功德自性尸羅，應知即是妙善淨戒，正受隨學，能利自他，利益安樂無量眾生，哀愍世間諸天人等，令得義利利益安樂故。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who possess these four qualities in their discipline's own intrinsic nature should be understood to hold a discipline both excellent and pure — properly received and then followed through in practice, able to benefit both self and others, bringing benefit and happiness to countless beings, out of compassion for gods and humans throughout the world, so that they attain genuine benefit and happiness.

items.zh: 應知即是無量淨戒，攝受無量菩薩所學故。應知即是饒益一切有情淨戒，現前能作一切有情利益安樂故。應知即是能獲大果勝利淨戒，攝受隨與無上正等菩提果故。是名菩薩自性戒。
items.en: It should be understood as a boundless pure discipline, gathering in everything countless bodhisattvas must learn. It should be understood as a pure discipline benefiting all beings, directly able to bring benefit and happiness to all beings. It should be understood as a pure discipline able to secure a great, supreme fruit, drawing one towards the fruit of unsurpassed, perfect awakening. This is called a bodhisattva's discipline in its intrinsic nature.

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切戒？

items.title: Section: Comprehensive Discipline Opens — Lay and Monastic, and Restraint's Seven Assemblies

items.zh: 謂菩薩戒略有二種。一、在家分戒，二、出家分戒。是名一切戒。又即依此在家、出家二分淨戒，略說三種。一、律儀戒，二、攝善法戒，三、饒益有情戒。
items.en: Bodhisattva discipline is, in brief, of two kinds: precepts for the householder portion, and precepts for the renunciant portion. This is called comprehensive discipline. And, resting on these same two portions of pure discipline, it may further, in brief, be described as three kinds: restraint discipline, discipline gathering wholesome practice, and discipline benefiting beings.

items.zh: 律儀戒者，謂諸菩薩所受七眾別解脫律儀。即是苾芻戒、苾芻尼戒、正學戒、勤策男戒、勤策女戒、近事男戒、近事女戒。如是七種，依止在家、出家二分，如應當知。是名菩薩律儀戒。
items.en: Restraint discipline means the individually liberating precepts of the seven assemblies that bodhisattvas receive: the monk's precepts, the nun's precepts, the female probationer's precepts, the male novice's precepts, the female novice's precepts, the male lay follower's precepts, and the female lay follower's precepts. These seven, resting respectively on the householder and renunciant portions, should be understood accordingly. This is called a bodhisattva's restraint discipline.

items.title: Section: Wholesome-Practice Precepts — Everything Done for Great Awakening, Rooted in Restraint

items.zh: 攝善法戒者，謂諸菩薩受律儀戒後，所有一切為大菩提，由身語意積集諸善，總說名為攝善法戒。
items.en: Discipline gathering wholesome practice means: bodhisattvas, having received restraint discipline, gather every wholesome quality of body, speech, and mind undertaken for the sake of great awakening — all of this together is called discipline gathering wholesome practice.

items.zh: 此復云何？
items.en: What is this again?

items.title: Section: Self-Generated Wholesome Practice — Hearing, Reflecting, and the Four Stages of Meditation

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩依戒、住戒，於聞、於思、於修止觀、於樂獨處精勤修學。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, resting on and abiding in discipline, diligently devote themselves to hearing the teaching, to reflecting on it, to cultivating calm-abiding and insight, and to delighting in solitude.

items.title: Wholesome Practice Generated Through Others Begins — Respecting One's Elders

items.zh: 如是時時於諸尊長精勤修習合掌、起迎、問訊、禮拜、恭敬之業，即於尊長勤修敬事。
items.en: In this way, again and again, one diligently practices, towards those senior in age and virtue, joining the palms, rising to greet them, inquiring after them, bowing, and other acts of respect — this is diligently cultivating reverent service towards one's elders.

items.title: Caring for the Sick, and Praising Genuinely Correct Teaching

items.zh: 於疾病者，悲愍殷重瞻侍供給。
items.en: Towards the sick, one attends and provides for them with compassion and earnest care.

items.zh: 於諸妙說，施以善哉。
items.en: Towards genuinely correct teaching, one offers genuine praise.

items.title: Genuine Praise for Virtue, and Rejoicing Aloud in Everyone's Merit

items.zh: 於有功德補特伽羅，真誠讚美。
items.en: Towards anyone possessing genuine virtue, one offers sincere, genuine praise.

items.zh: 於十方界一切有情一切福業，以勝意樂起淨信心發言隨喜。
items.en: Towards every wholesome deed performed by any being throughout the ten directions, one gives rise to pure faith through an elevated intention, and expresses that rejoicing aloud.

items.title: Section: Bearing Others' Wrongs — Five Contemplations That Make Genuine Patience Possible

items.zh: 於他所作一切違犯，思擇安忍。
items.en: Towards whatever offence another commits, one carefully reflects and patiently endures.

items.title: Section: Dedicating Every Wholesome Root to Awakening Itself

items.zh: 以身語意已作、未作一切善根，迴向無上正等菩提，時時發起種種正願。
items.en: One dedicates every wholesome root of body, speech, and mind, whether already accomplished or not yet accomplished, towards unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and again and again gives rise to various genuine vows.

items.title: Offering to the Three Jewels With Six Kinds of Elevated Intention

items.zh: 以一切種上妙供具，供佛法僧。
items.en: One offers every kind of fine, precious object in devotion to the Buddha, the teaching, and the community.

items.title: Diligent Cultivation of Every Wholesome Practice

items.zh: 於諸善品，恒常勇猛精進修習。
items.en: Towards every wholesome quality, one constantly and courageously cultivates with diligence.

items.title: Section: Protecting Wholesome Practice — Five Supports From Vigilance to Nightly Cultivation

items.zh: 於身語意住不放逸。於諸學處，正念正知。正行防守，密護根門。
items.en: One abides in vigilance over body, speech, and mind. Regarding what one has studied, one holds clear mindfulness and awareness. Acting rightly, one guards and carefully protects the sense doors.

items.zh: 於食知量。初夜後夜常修覺悟。
items.en: One knows the right measure in eating. In the first and last watches of the night, one constantly cultivates wakeful practice.

items.title: Increasing Wholesome Practice — Association With Genuinely Good Friends

items.zh: 親近善士，依止善友。
items.en: One draws close to genuinely good people, and relies on good friends.

blocks.text: Fascicle 40 is the famous **chapter on moral discipline** (戒品) of the Bodhisattva Stage: the source of the "three storehouses of pure precepts" (三聚淨戒) and of the bodhisattva vows still taken today, especially in the Tibetan tradition. It follows the same nine-part frame as giving.

Intrinsic nature, comprehensive, difficult, every gateway, a good person's, every kind, fulfilling requests, bringing joy now and later, pure. Master Cháng Bǎi: it is hard to receive, hard to keep, and hard to keep well.

Discipline is: **properly received from another**; held with **a good and pure aspiration**; **purified again after a lapse**; and kept with **deep reverence and focused mindfulness, without violation**. Venerable Miào Jìng: proper reception is the outer condition; pure aspiration, the inner.

Having received from another, one feels shame before others (愧) if one breaks it; holding it with pure aspiration, shame before oneself (慚). Confessing a lapse, or never lapsing, one is free of remorse. Master Cháng Bǎi: to keep regretting after confessing is itself a delusion.

"A boundless pure discipline gathering everything countless bodhisattvas must learn." **Restraint** (律儀戒): the prātimokṣa precepts of the seven assemblies, monks to lay followers. **Gathering wholesome practice** (攝善法戒): every good of body, speech, and mind done for awakening. **Benefiting beings** (饒益有情戒). Master Cháng Bǎi: a monk may give back his monastic precepts, but the bodhisattva precepts continue.

Hearing, reflecting, calm and insight, solitude; respecting elders; caring for the sick; praising correct teaching and genuine virtue; rejoicing aloud in others' merit; "patiently enduring others' offences"; dedicating every root of good to awakening (Venerable Miào Jìng: make concrete plans: "within five years I will…"); offerings to the Three Jewels; diligence; vigilance; moderation in food; wakefulness; good friends; and honestly seeing one's own faults and confessing them.

quiz.q: Of the nine aspects, why is "difficult discipline" difficult, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: hard to receive, hard to guard, and keeping what is hard to keep
it costs a lot of money
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it is hard at the time of receiving, hard in guarding the precepts, and it means keeping what is hard to keep — hence "difficult."

quiz.q: How do the two lectures distinguish "properly received from another" from "a good and pure aspiration"?
options: both: the aspiration is the external condition

Miào Jìng: proper reception is the external condition, the aspiration the inner pure wish; Cháng Bǎi: proper reception belongs to the mental factor of receiving, the aspiration to the factor of desire
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: proper reception is the external condition for receiving the precepts; the good and pure aspiration is the inner pure wish of the one receiving. Master Cháng Bǎi: proper reception is the mental factor of receiving; the aspiration is the mental factor of desire. Miào Jìng says the same at §7.

quiz.q: Through two causes bodhisattvas are "freed of lingering remorse." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say about someone who keeps regretting even after confession?
options: continuing to regret after confession is simply delusion
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if after confessing one keeps on regretting, that is delusion; lingering remorse obstructs the cultivation of calm.

quiz.q: The treatise distinguishes outward "kuì" from inward "cán," but the English renders both as "shame." How do the lectures distinguish them?
options: fear of punishment vs. fear of losing money
kuì is shame from reverent awe towards others (outward); cán is shame from one's own reflection (inward)
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: shame arising from reverence and awe towards other spiritual friends is kuì; shame from reflecting on one's own violation is cán. Venerable Miào Jìng: cán is inward. The English does not carry the distinction.

quiz.q: Resting on the householder and renunciant portions, which three kinds of discipline does the treatise describe?
options: restraint discipline, discipline gathering wholesome practice, discipline benefiting beings
quiz.why: "Resting on these same two portions of pure discipline, it may further be described as three kinds: restraint discipline, discipline gathering wholesome practice, and discipline benefiting beings." Venerable Miào Jìng: avoiding all evil is restraint; accomplishing all wholesome roots is gathering wholesome practice.

quiz.q: All seven assemblies may receive the bodhisattva precepts. According to Master Cháng Bǎi, what happens to a monk's bodhisattva precepts if he gives up the monastic precepts and returns to lay life?
options: the bodhisattva precepts remain; he is still a householder bodhisattva
he must reordain to keep them
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: he gives up the monk's precepts and returns to lay life, but the bodhisattva precepts he received remain — he is still a householder bodhisattva. Venerable Miào Jìng: the bodhisattva precepts last to the end of the future; even when this life ends, they are not lost.

quiz.q: "Towards whatever offence another commits, one carefully reflects and patiently endures." What five contemplations does Master Cháng Bǎi list?
options: the contemplation of mere phenomena, of former kinship, of impermanence, of suffering, and of embracing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one cultivates the contemplations of mere phenomena, of former kinship, of impermanence, of suffering, and of embracing. Venerable Miào Jìng on former kinship: these offending beings may in a past life have been your siblings, close friends, or even parents.
